pr.title: Don't treat asserts as a call in cross-crate inlining
pr.description: Making functions with calls in their bodies automatically cross-crate-inlinable tends to tank incremental build times. Though assert terminators are _like_ calls, they don't exhibit the same behavior.
pr.author: saethlin

classification.name: Inline
evidence: The shared cross-crate-inlinability query changed in the PR is consumed by the concrete `Inline` MirPass: inspected `inline.rs` shows `NormalInliner::check_callee_mir_body` using `tcx.cross_crate_inlinable(...)` to choose the inline threshold, so changing assert handling changes which callees `Inline` will inline.

analysis.originalLogic: In `CostChecker::visit_terminator`, an assert terminator was charged to the call budget: `TerminatorKind::Assert { unwind, .. } => { self.calls += 1; ... }`, while ordinary terminator cost was added only by the catch-all `_ => self.statements += 1`. `cross_crate_inlinable` compares these counters against a threshold; calls are penalized because they make a function non-leaf and can grow incremental CGUs, whereas assertions are only assert-like.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Classify each `TerminatorKind::Assert` as a call by incrementing `calls` instead of treating it as an ordinary statement. In the bad model, a small leaf callee whose optimized MIR contains an assert (e.g. `a / b`, which lowers to a division plus an assert) exhausts the call budget, so `cross_crate_inlinable` rejects it and the downstream `Inline` pass leaves the call site un-inlined. The corrected transformation increments `statements` for every terminator unconditionally, does not increment `calls` for `Assert`, and keeps genuine calls (`TerminatorKind::Call` and `TerminatorKind::TailCall`) charged to `calls`. Removing the assert's call cost without adding it to `statements` would instead undercount its cost.
analysis.inputDomain: Optimized MIR of cross-crate-inlining candidates, especially small dependency/sysroot functions containing `Assert` terminators but no real calls (e.g. integer division / bounds checks), evaluated by `cross_crate_inlinable` and then consumed by the `Inline` pass in a downstream crate. The relevant compile-time configuration includes the cross-crate inline threshold; an explicit `-Zcross-crate-inline-threshold=never` disables this path.
analysis.summary: Historical Rust PR correcting the cost model used by `cross_crate_inlinable`: `Assert` terminators were charged as calls, preventing small assert-containing leaf functions from being cross-crate-inlined. The fix treats asserts as statements and adds `TailCall` to the real-call category, improving inlining without the incremental-CGU blowup caused by genuinely call-containing functions.
analysis.trigger: A cross-crate-inlining candidate has one or more `Assert` terminators in its optimized MIR but no genuine calls. Under the old classification the assert increments `calls`, so the candidate can fail the call threshold and `cross_crate_inlinable` returns false; under the corrected classification the assert costs only a statement, so the candidate qualifies and `Inline` can inline the call.
preconditions: The callee is in another crate (dependency or sysroot) and is being considered by `cross_crate_inlinable`/the `Inline` pass.
Its optimized MIR contains `TerminatorKind::Assert` (for example, the divisor-nonzero assert emitted for `a / b`).
The calls threshold is restrictive enough that the old misclassification changes the inlinability result.
The cost counter must still account for the assert as a statement after it is removed from the call count.
Genuine `Call` and `TailCall` terminators must remain charged as calls; they are not assert-like.
pitfalls: Do not conflate `Assert` with `Call`: the PR description states asserts are only like calls and do not have the same incremental-build impact.

The correction is not simply deleting `self.calls += 1`; the patch also moves `self.statements += 1` to the top of `visit_terminator` so every terminator, including `Assert`, still contributes statement cost.
Do not classify every unusual terminator as assert-like: `TerminatorKind::TailCall { .. }` is newly treated as a real call.
`FalseUnwind`, `FalseEdge`, `Yield`, and `CoroutineDrop` are treated as impossible in runtime MIR via `bug!`, rather than silently assigned costs.
The observed change is missed inlining/IR shape, not miscompilation; do not claim execution or reproduction was performed.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the codegen-LLVM cross-crate-inlining test layout: an auxiliary `leaf` crate exposes `pub fn leaf_with_assert(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 { a / b }`, and the outer crate calls it through `#[no_mangle] pub fn leaf_with_assert`. FileCheck assertions `CHECK-NOT: call {{.*}}leaf_with_assert` and `CHECK: sdiv i32 %a, %b` verify that the assert-containing callee was inlined. To construct the two differing programs, compile identical source with the old cost classification (assert increments calls) versus the corrected one (assert increments statements); only the inlining decision/IR should differ. Keep the item-collection test isolated with `//@ compile-flags: -Zcross-crate-inline-threshold=never`, as the patch does, so implicit panic-call collection is not accidentally affected by cross-crate inlining. This is a static codegen/FileCheck strategy; no compiler run is claimed here.
